title: 辩论：物质极度丰裕后，人会走向衰亡吗？
title_en: Does material abundance lead to decline?

questions.question: 卡尔霍恩本人如何解读他那个「老鼠乌托邦」的崩溃？
options: 食物和水供应过剩，导致代谢疾病在鼠群中大面积蔓延
缺的是位置：角色被先来者占满，新一代无处成为任何人
没有天敌和挑战，种群的基因质量在几代之内持续退化
种群过度拥挤、远远超出了围场设计的容量，长期的应激最终压垮了整个群体
questions.explanation: 卡尔霍恩强调峰值约两千二百只，远低于三千八百的容量，不缺食物也不缺空间，缺的是「还没有人做过的事」。他认为一个社会先耗尽的是可当的角色，而不是资源，所以把实验读成「富足会毁掉我们」是把结论念反了。
questions.question_en: How did Calhoun himself interpret the collapse of his "mouse utopia"?
options_en: An oversupply of food and water led to widespread metabolic disease in the colony
What ran out was positions: every social role was taken by earlier arrivals, leaving the new generation nowhere to become anyone
With no predators or challenges, the population's genetic quality degraded within a few generations
Overcrowding far beyond the enclosure's designed capacity created chronic stress that finally broke the colony
questions.explanation_en: Calhoun stresses the population peaked around 2,200, far below the 3,800 capacity — no shortage of food or space; what was missing was "things no one had done yet." A society runs out of roles before resources, he argues, so reading the experiment as "abundance destroys us" gets his conclusion backwards.

questions.question: 凯恩斯解释自己「一周工作十五小时」的预言为何落空，给出的理由是什么？
options: 生产率的实际增长远远低于他当年的估计，所以人们身上的经济压力从未真正解除
资本方持续压低工资，迫使工人不得不靠加班来维持生活
人天生热爱工作，一旦闲暇过多反而会陷入焦虑和失落
相对需要只在高人一头时才满足、永不饱和，丰裕给了它更大的赛场
questions.explanation: 凯恩斯说产出那一半猜得相当准，错的是工时。他早分过两种需要：绝对需要会饱和，相对需要永不知足；丰裕解决了第一种，却为第二种扩大了赛场，所以生产力红利几乎全兑换成了更多东西，没有兑换成时间。
questions.question_en: Why, according to Keynes, did his prediction of a fifteen-hour workweek fail?
options_en: Actual productivity growth fell far short of his estimate, so people's economic pressure never really lifted
Employers kept wages down, forcing workers to rely on overtime to get by
People inherently love work, and too much leisure leaves them anxious and lost
Relative needs are satisfied only by being above others and never saturate; abundance just gave them a bigger arena
questions.explanation_en: Keynes says he got output roughly right and hours badly wrong. He had distinguished absolute needs, which saturate, from relative needs, which never do; abundance met the first but enlarged the arena for the second, so productivity gains were cashed out almost entirely in more stuff rather than more time.

questions.question: 凯恩斯为什么认为伊壁鸠鲁「替他减去欲望」的办法不能当公共政策？
options: 欲望本身就是幸福的来源，减少欲望只会让人变得更不快乐
欲望是创新的根本动力，大规模减欲会在长期拖累技术进步与整体生活水平
减欲违背人性，绝大多数人根本做不到，劝了也没有用
人人同时减欲会让需求坍塌、工厂关门，造成失业
questions.explanation: 这就是凯恩斯说的节俭悖论：个人美德加总起来可能是集体灾难，省下来的不会变成宁静，会变成失业。他说这是一道分配与制度的题，不是修养题，处方是更短的工时和更好的图书馆、球场。他承认减欲作为个人处方「极好」。
questions.question_en: Why does Keynes say Epicurus's remedy of "subtracting desires" can't serve as public policy?
options_en: Desire is itself the source of happiness, so reducing it would only make people less happy
Desire is the root driver of innovation, so mass desire-reduction would drag down technology and living standards over time
Reducing desire goes against human nature; most people simply can't do it, so urging them is pointless
If everyone cut desires at once, demand would collapse and factories would close, causing unemployment
questions.explanation_en: This is Keynes's paradox of thrift: individual virtue summed up can be collective disaster — the savings become unemployment, not tranquility. He frames it as a problem of distribution and institutions, not self-cultivation, prescribing shorter hours and better libraries and playing fields. He calls desire-reduction an excellent personal prescription.
